title: Savya
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In Yevamot 16a and 16b: “Rabbi Yochanan and Savya both say.” And there at 86b: “Rabbi Yonatan and Savya disagree about it”; Hyman infers from the latter passage that Savya is a sage’s name.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Hyman lists Yevamot 16a and 16b separately; these are not asserted to be a continuous quotation spanning the folio boundary. His inference that Savya is a sage’s name is preserved as his inference; the William Davidson 86b paragraph has Yonatan and Savya disagreeing.

The William Davidson text has Rabbi Yochanan and Savya “both say” at Yevamot 16a, but introduces a disagreement between them at 16b; 86b has Rabbi Yonatan and Savya disagreeing. Hyman’s compressed references and personal-name inference are retained without treating all three passages as one continuous quotation or resolving Savya to an authority identity.
